{{Quote|The Vagabond is the one Hour who can never enter the Mansus, but she goes everywhere else... and, if you believe her boasts, she's the only one who knows all the Histories. Sometimes, she lets someone record her travels.|Vagabond's Map}}
'''The Vagabond''', also called '''The Centipede''', '''The Laughingthrush''', '''The Sight-Thief''', '''The Proverbial Footloose''', '''The Pilgrim''', and many other names, is one of the [[Hours]], associated with hour XVII, or 5:00pm. Her [[Aspects]] are {{Lore|Moth}} and possibly {{Lore|Secret Histories}}. The Vagabond is a God-from-Flesh, and the only Hour who does not dwell in the [[Mansus]].

According to ''[[The Book of Masks]]'', The Vagabond was born in a place called [[Miah]], where she was punished for entering its temple-precinct. Sometime after ascending to Hour-hood, she took her revenge on Miah as The Centipede by cursing it "to drink only dust and to be remembered only by the wind". As The Laughingthrush, she was a friend of [[The Sun-in-Splendour]] before his division. As The Sight-Thief, she created [[Way: Through the Stag Door#The Painted River|The Painted River]] in the Mansus. As The Vagabond, she has been barred from the Mansus for some incident that has yet to occur.

In ''[[Where Has She Gone?]]'', it is claimed that The Vagabond has traveled all nine continents, the Mansus, the [[Way: The Wood|Wood]], and places forbidden to other Hours. She has also already visited [[Nowhere]] and "will not return", yet her ultimate goal is to visit [[The Glory]].

In ''[[The Serenity of the Black Wood]]'', the Vagabond leads several travelers in [[Way: The Wood|a wood]] and abandons them part-way. It is strongly implied that those travelers founded [[Obliviates|the House of Lethe.]]

According to ''[[In The Mountains...|In the Mountains]]'', the Vagabond sometimes takes the bird-form and meets with the [[The Elegiast|Ivory Dove]], the [[The Beachcomber|Beachcrow]] and the [[The Witch-and-Sister|Witch-and-Sister]] on a mountaintop to exchange gossip unheard by their peers. Sometimes, a mortal overhears them and is subsequently destroyed, and the meeting place of those Hours is changed. In ''[[The Book of the White Cat]]'', the woman known as Penelope of Gordian claims that her cat spies on their meetings in the mountains north of [[wikipedia:Gordion|Gordion]].

She will be the first of the seven pilgrims in the [[The Door in the Eye|Watchman]]'s [[The Watchman's Pilgrimage|Pilgrimage]].
